title: Deadlocks
analogy: Two Jack-o'-Gobblers sit around a bubbling Halloween cauldron, each clutching a bone ladle and waiting for the other's potion bowl. Neither lets go, so neither drinks!
concept: A deadlock happens when processes wait on each other forever. It requires four conditions at once: mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, and circular wait. Break any one and deadlock cannot occur, for example by ordering resources so everyone grabs them in the same sequence.

quiz.q: Which condition is needed for deadlock?
quiz.why: Circular wait means each Jack-o'-Gobbler waits on the next monster's ladle.

quiz.q: How does acquiring resources in a fixed global order help?
quiz.why: If every monster reaches for the ladle first, then the potion bowl, no cycle can form.
